units.title: Wasserstein distance transfers a Lipschitz observable's second moment
units.boundary: Ordinary quadratic Wasserstein cost only. No optimal coupling, twisted metric, probability normalization, phase history or SPHMC convergence theorem is asserted.

sources.label: SPHMC Lemma D.4 prerequisite
sources.scope: Samplinglib-authored expansion of the standard transport step used after (D.3).

assumptions: E is a second-countable Borel normed additive group and F is a normed additive group.
g:E→F is b-Lipschitz and its squared norm is integrable under the reference law ν.
The squared extended-real Wasserstein distance from μ to ν is at most ofReal(r²).
units.statement: The observable remains square-integrable under μ, and its μ second moment is bounded by twice its reference second moment plus 2b²r².

steps.title: Choose an almost-optimal coupling
steps.text: For every s>r², the definition of transport cost supplies a coupling whose quadratic cost is below s. Optimal-plan existence is unnecessary.

steps.title: Dominate the transported observable
steps.text: Lipschitz continuity and the quadratic two-term inequality control the first-coordinate observable by an integrable reference term plus coupling displacement.
steps.lean: The private pointwise bound and Integrable.mono' establish integrability before integral comparison.

steps.title: Use the exact marginals
steps.text: The coordinate projections of γ preserve μ and ν, so the two coupling integrals are exactly the desired marginal moments.

steps.title: Remove the excess cost
steps.text: The bound holds for every s>r². Applying it at a controlled positive excess and letting that excess be arbitrary gives the closed r² bound.
steps.lean: le_of_forall_pos_le_add and real algebra close the infimum argument.

units.lean_statement: The statement explicitly returns Integrable before its real-valued integral inequality.
units.lean_proof: Approximate coupling, pointwise quadratic domination, marginal pushforward identities, then an epsilon closure argument.

units.title: Ordinary-Wasserstein control gives an SPHMC phase-state moment
units.boundary: The premise uses Lean's ordinary product max metric, not the paper's M_kappa metric. The theorem does not prove (D.3), a run-history invariant, layer-center moments, (D.7) or (D.8).

sources.label: Chen–Chewi–Lu–Zhang, Lemma D.4 proof
sources.scope: The phase-state second-moment transition after (D.3), with the metric comparison intentionally left separate.

assumptions: The reference phase law has integrable position and momentum squares, bounded respectively by Mx and Mp.
The incoming law is within ordinary squared W2 radius r² of the reference law.
The state space is finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel; completeness is not needed by this theorem.
units.statement: The incoming phase energy is integrable and at most 2(Mx+Mp)+4r².

steps.title: Position is a one-Lipschitz observable
steps.text: For the max product metric, projecting to position and subtracting xstar cannot increase distance.

steps.title: Momentum is a one-Lipschitz observable
steps.text: The second product projection is one-Lipschitz for the same metric.

steps.title: Transfer both moments
steps.text: Apply the shared theorem independently to position and momentum, preserving both integrability conclusions.

steps.title: Add only after integrability
steps.text: Bochner integral additivity is now legal; adding the bounds gives the combined phase energy.

units.lean_statement: The metric and every reference moment premise are visible; no stationary-law or history premise is hidden.
units.lean_proof: Instantiate the shared observable theorem with the two phase projections and add the resulting integrable moments.
